time.tuning_note: 8 actions per loop is a first test value (decision Q3). Shortest Loop 1 escape is 5 actions.

background.text: You booked one last stay before the inn closes for good.
background.use: Only if a scene needs a reason for you being here.

description.text: A small room under the eaves. The radiator ticks, the quilt is heavy, and the frosted window looks down on a snowy garden.

examine.text: A plain wooden door. This is where the envelope was waiting this morning.
A plain wooden door. The floor in front of it is bare this morning.
Under a folded spare blanket you find an old photograph, its corners soft with age.
Snow blankets the garden below. You can make out a back gate in the hedge. It's a long drop, though. The stairs would be wiser.

description.text: The heart of the inn: worn armchairs, a crackling fire, and a tall grandfather clock that ticks a little louder than it should.

examine.text: Polished walnut and a slow brass pendulum, the case tall enough to hide a child. Words are carved into the base.
The pendulum swings, slow and steady, just as before.
A brass bell, the guest book, and a neatly printed notice. You take the notice.
The bell and the guest book. The bell gleams; someone polishes it every day.
Snow is banked halfway up the glass. Nobody is leaving this way until tomorrow.
The innkeeper cuts you a slice, still warm. Buttery crust, a little too much cinnamon in exactly the right way.
You've already had a slice. You consider a second. You're only human.

unavailable_text.text: No pie yet. The innkeeper serves it in the evening.

description.text: A walled garden asleep under snow: a hedge, a few stubborn bushes, terracotta flowerpots, and an iron back gate.

examine.text: The key turns with a stiff click. The gate swings open onto a lane that winds away into the snow.
An iron gate in the hedge, locked tight.
An iron gate in the hedge, locked tight. Beyond it, a lane winds away from the inn.
A torn scrap of blue ribbon is caught on the thorns, faded by many winters. You work it free.
You tip the flowerpot. Underneath, pressed into the frozen soil, is a small iron key.

gate_key.journal_fact: The gate key was under the flowerpot.

closing_notice.journal_fact: The inn closes for good tomorrow.

blue_ribbon.name: Torn blue ribbon
blue_ribbon.journal_fact: A torn blue ribbon was caught on a garden bush.

description.text: The innkeeper and a little girl with a blue ribbon, beside the clock.

old_photo.journal_fact: The old photo shows the innkeeper and a little girl with a blue ribbon, beside the clock.

clock_inscription.name: Clock inscription

text.text: Mind the hours you wish away.

text_options_for_designer: Mind the hours you wish away.
Every hour I keep, I keep for you.
Wind me gently. I am listening.

innkeeper.name: Innkeeper

intro.text: The innkeeper: a kind, tired man in a cardigan, who looks at his inn the way some people look at old friends.

knows: He made a "silly wish" at the clock last night.
A little girl once lived here long ago.

presence.text: The innkeeper is winding the grandfather clock, humming to himself.
The innkeeper is behind the reception desk, polishing the bell.
The innkeeper is cutting slices of pie by the fire.

fallback.text: He turns it over, smiles kindly, and hands it back. "Can't say I know what to make of that, I'm afraid."

mira.name: Mira

intro.text: Mira: a fellow guest in a bright scarf, who moves around the inn as if she knows every creaky board.

knows: She is the girl from the photo.
Her plan for tomorrow: reveal who she is and take over the inn.
senses: Déjà vu she cannot explain: she senses the loop but barely recalls anything.

presence.text: Mira is curled up in an armchair by the fire.
Mira is wandering the garden, brushing snow off the hedge.
Mira sits by the fire with a cup of tea.
Mira stands in the snowy garden, looking up at the lit windows.

night.activity: waits to tell the innkeeper who she is

presence.text: Mira sits beside the grandfather clock, waiting for someone who doesn't come.

schedule_triggers.purpose: Puts Mira near the clock at midnight (memory trigger).

first_meeting_line.note: Her first line in each loop, the first time the player meets her (normally the Lobby, Morning).

lines: You're new here. Try the pie tonight; it's the best thing about this place.

narration.text: Mira looks up from her armchair and smiles.

ambient.trigger: Player examines back_gate without the key while Mira is present.
ambient.intent: Mira mentions the key is under the flowerpot (another hint that she knows the inn too well).
ambient.text: Mira glances over. "Locked? The key's under the flowerpot. Always has been." She blinks, as if surprised she knew that.
ambient.journal_fact: Mira knew the gate key was under the flowerpot.

ambient.trigger: Loop 2+, after Mira was near the clock at the previous midnight; player examines the grandfather clock while Mira is present.
ambient.intent: A vague myth about the clock. Must not state the rule (pillar 2).
ambient.text: "There was a story about this clock, when I was small," Mira says. "Something about being careful what you tell it." She shrugs. "I don't remember the rest."
ambient.journal_fact: Mira remembers a story about being careful what you tell the clock.

fallback.text: Mira tilts her head. "Hm. Should that mean something to me?"

reactions.intent: Found it in the clock this morning while winding it. Points at the clock.
reactions.text: "Ah, that! It was tucked inside the clock when I wound it this morning. Had your name on it, so I slipped it under your door." He nods at the grandfather clock.
reactions.journal_fact: The innkeeper found the note in the clock.

reactions.intent: He has never seen it (the player carried it through midnight, so it wasn't in the clock). Decision Q5.
reactions.text: He squints at the envelope. "Your name, but I've never seen it before. Did someone leave it for you?"
reactions.journal_fact: The innkeeper says he has never seen the note.

reactions.intent: Puzzled; mild déjà vu about midnight.
reactions.text: Mira reads the line twice. "Midnight…" She laughs, a little uncertain. "Funny. For a second that felt familiar."
reactions.journal_fact: Mira said the note felt familiar.

reactions.intent: Sad; wishes today would never end. (Hint of the wish.)
reactions.text: He sighs. "All these years. Sometimes I think, if today could just… not end." He shakes his head. "Listen to me."
reactions.journal_fact: The innkeeper wishes today would never end.

narration.text: Mira taps the notice and smiles.

reactions.journal_fact: Mira says tomorrow might surprise you.

reactions.intent: Reminds him of a little girl who stayed here long ago.
reactions.text: "Blue ribbon… There was a little girl here once, long ago. Wore one just like it, every single day." He smiles at nothing for a moment.
reactions.journal_fact: A little girl with a blue ribbon once lived at the inn.

reactions.text: Mira's hand drifts toward it, then stops. She looks away. "Is it me, or is the snow getting heavier?"
reactions.journal_fact: Mira changed the subject when shown the ribbon.

reactions.intent: Nostalgic about the girl; does not connect her to Mira.
reactions.text: "Where did you find this? That's me, believe it or not. And that's the little girl who lived here." He runs a thumb over the edge. "I wonder what became of her."
reactions.journal_fact: The innkeeper doesn't know what became of the girl in the photo.

reactions.intent: TRIGGER: goes quiet, decides it is time to tell him.
reactions.text: Mira goes very quiet. She looks at the photo for a long time. "I think," she says softly, "it's time I told him something."
reactions.journal_fact: Mira wants to tell the innkeeper something.

reactions.intent: Deflects; admits he "said something silly to that clock last night".
reactions.text: He chuckles, a little pink. "Oh, that old thing. I said something silly to that clock last night. Don't tell anyone."
reactions.locked_fragment: said something silly to that clock last night
reactions.journal_fact: The innkeeper said something to the clock last night.

reactions.intent: Says she used to hide inside its case as a child.
reactions.text: "I used to hide in there, you know. Right inside the case, with the pendulum going tick, tick above my head." She stops. "When I was little."
reactions.journal_fact: Mira used to hide inside the clock's case as a child.

reaction_fallbacks.uncovered_combination: Use the target NPC's fallback line.
reaction_fallbacks.target_not_present: Cannot happen: actions() only lists NPCs in the player's location.

present_to_location.text: You hold up the {item}. The {place} keeps its thoughts to itself.

reset.effect: Everything resets to the morning of the same day: locations, NPC schedules (including triggers), items, flags.

keepers: Anyone in the Lobby (near the clock) at the moment of midnight.
Anyone carrying an anchored object at midnight.

anchoring.rule: Objects inside or touching the clock at midnight persist through the reset.

note_lifecycle.loop_1: The innkeeper found the sealed envelope in the clock while winding it, didn't open it, saw the player's name and slid it under the player's door. Auto-picked up on waking.
note_lifecycle.loop_2_plus: The player carried the note through midnight, so it stays in their inventory. Nothing is under the door and the clock is empty.

rules.escape: Opening the back gate with the key ends the loop immediately and plays the escape midnight scene.
rules.loop_cannot_end: The wisher does not know the wish came true, so the loop never ends (MVP: no ending; see end_conditions).

wake.text: You wake under a heavy quilt. Grey winter light, the smell of coffee from downstairs. On the floor inside the door lies an envelope with your name on it. You open it. One line: "Leave before midnight."
You wake under the same heavy quilt. Grey winter light. The smell of coffee. The floor by the door is bare, but the envelope is still in your pocket.
wake.thought: Again? Something about this day won't let go.

wake.text: You wake under the same heavy quilt. Grey winter light. The smell of coffee. The floor by the door is bare, but the envelope is still in your pocket.
wake.thought: Something isn't right. What happened last night, and why?

escaped.intent: While walking away, the clock's chime sounds as if right beside the player; the inn is ahead again.
escaped.text: You follow the lane into the snow. The inn's lights shrink behind you. Then, close enough to touch, a clock begins to chime. Twelve. You look up. The inn is ahead of you again, every window glowing.
escaped.fade: The snow tilts, the lights blur, and everything goes quiet.

in_lobby.lead_in: The fire burns low, and you lose track of time.
in_lobby.text: The grandfather clock strikes twelve. The sound fills the room, fills your chest, fills everything.
in_lobby.fade: Your knees go soft. The last thing you hear is the pendulum.

elsewhere.lead_in: You lose track of time. The inn goes quiet around you, one light at a time.
elsewhere.text: Somewhere in the inn, faint and far away, a clock strikes twelve. The world around you goes soft.
elsewhere.fade: Your eyes grow heavy. You don't remember lying down.

intended_path: learn of the back gate and key
loop_1.player_memory: The player remembers from Loop 1 onward because they carry the anchored note at midnight.
